coach.unterminatedString.what: A piece of text (a string) was opened with a quote but never closed on the same line.
coach.unterminatedString.fix: Add the matching closing quote at the end of the text. Use the same kind of quote (' or ") that you opened with.
coach.unterminatedTriple.what: A text opened with three quotes was never closed.
coach.unterminatedTriple.fix: Close it with the same three quotes.
coach.expectedColon.what: Python expected a colon (:) at the end of this line, after if, for, while, def or class.
coach.expectedColon.fix: Put a : at the end of the line, then indent the lines that belong to it.
coach.brackets.what: A bracket ( [ or { was opened and never closed, or a closing one has no partner.
coach.brackets.fix: Count your brackets on this line and the lines above it. Every opening one needs a closing one.
coach.assignInCondition.what: You wrote = (store a value) where a comparison was meant.
coach.assignInCondition.fix: To ask whether two things are equal, use == (two equal signs).
coach.cannotAssign.what: You cannot store a value into {what}. The left side of = must be a name.
coach.cannotAssign.fix: Put a name on the left, for example total = 5. Use == to compare.
coach.syntaxGeneric.what: Python could not understand this line: something is written in a way Python does not allow.
coach.syntaxGeneric.fix: Look closely at the line shown, and the one before it. Check for a missing comma, colon, quote or bracket, and for typos in keywords.
coach.expectedIndent.what: A line that ends with a colon needs its body indented underneath it, and there is none.
coach.expectedIndent.fix: Indent the next line by 4 spaces. If the body is not ready, write pass on that line for now.
coach.unexpectedIndent.what: This line is indented but nothing above it asks for an indent.
coach.unexpectedIndent.fix: Remove the extra spaces at the start of the line so it lines up with the one above.
coach.unindentMismatch.what: The indentation of this line does not match any earlier level.
coach.unindentMismatch.fix: Use the same number of spaces (4 is the habit) for lines that belong together.
coach.indentGeneric.fix: Use only spaces, and the same number for lines in the same block.
coach.nameNotDefined.what: Python does not know the name {name}. It has not been given a value yet, or it is spelled differently.
coach.nameNotDefined.fix: Check the spelling and the capital letters: names are case-sensitive. Make sure the line that creates {name} comes before this line. Text needs quotes, for example "hello".
coach.unboundLocal.what: Inside this function, {name} is treated as a local name, but it is used before it was given a value.
coach.unboundLocal.fix: Give {name} a value inside the function before using it, or pass it in as a parameter.
coach.concatStr.what: You tried to join text with a {other} using +. Python does not mix them.
coach.concatStr.fix: Turn the number into text with str(), or use an f-string.
coach.badOperands.what: The operator {op} cannot combine a {a} and a {b}.
coach.badOperands.fix: Convert one side so both are the same kind, for example int("5") turns text into a number and str(5) turns a number into text.
coach.notSubscriptable.what: You used [ ] on a {type}, but a {type} has no positions or keys to look up.
coach.notSubscriptable.fix: Check that the value is the list, string, tuple or dictionary you expect. A number or None cannot be indexed.
coach.notCallable.what: You put parentheses after a {type}, as if it were a function, but it is not one.
coach.notCallable.fix: Remove the parentheses, or check that you did not reuse the name of a function for a value (for example sum = 5 and then sum(...)).
coach.notIterable.what: A for loop or a function wanted something it can go through item by item, but got a {type}.
coach.notIterable.fix: Use range(n) to count with a number, or make sure the value is a list, string, tuple, set or dictionary.
coach.noItemAssign.what: A {type} cannot be changed in place by assigning to a position.
coach.noItemAssign.fix: Strings and tuples are immutable. Build a new one instead, or convert to a list, change it, and convert back.
coach.argCount.what: {fn} was called with {got} value(s) but it accepts {want}.
coach.argCount.fix: Count the parameters in the def line and the values in the call; they must match.
coach.argMissing.what: {fn} needs {n} more value(s) than it was given.
coach.argMissing.fix: Pass a value for every parameter in the def line, or give the parameter a default value.
coach.strNeeded.what: An operation expected text (or a whole number) and got a different kind of value.
coach.strNeeded.fix: Convert the value first: str(...) for text, int(...) for a whole number.
coach.indexType.what: A position inside [ ] must be a whole number (or a slice like 1:3).
coach.indexType.fix: Use an int. If the number came from input() or a division, convert it with int(...) or use //.
coach.typeGeneric.what: An operation was used on a value of the wrong kind.
coach.typeGeneric.fix: Print the values involved with print(type(x)) to see what they really are.
coach.intLiteral.what: int() was given {text}, which is not written as a whole number.
coach.intLiteral.fix: Make sure the text holds only digits (and maybe a leading minus). Spaces and decimals like 3.5 are not accepted; use float() for decimals.
coach.floatLiteral.what: float() was given {text}, which is not a number.
coach.floatLiteral.fix: Check the text holds a number such as 3.5, with a dot rather than a comma.
coach.unpackCount.what: The number of names on the left does not match the number of values on the right.
coach.unpackCount.fix: Count both sides. Use a starred name (first, *rest = values) to collect the extras.
coach.notInList.what: You asked for a value that is not in the list.
coach.notInList.fix: Check with  x in my_list  first, or print the list to see what it holds.
coach.valueGeneric.what: The value has the right kind but is not acceptable here.
coach.valueGeneric.fix: Read the message below: it names the value Python rejected.
coach.indexRange.what: You asked for a position that does not exist. Positions start at 0 and the last one is length minus 1.
coach.indexRange.fix: Print len(...) to see the size, and use an index from 0 up to len(...) - 1, or -1 for the last item.
coach.keyMissing.fix: Check the spelling and capitals of the key, or use d.get(key) which gives None instead of an error.
coach.zeroDiv.what: You divided by zero, which is not possible.
coach.zeroDiv.fix: Check the value you divide by before dividing, for example with an if.
coach.noAttribute.what: A {type} has no feature (attribute or method) called {attr}.
coach.noAttribute.fix: Check the spelling, and that the value is the kind you think it is: print(type(x)). Lists have append, sets have add, strings have upper.
coach.noModule.what: Python cannot find a module called {name}.
coach.noModule.fix: Check the spelling. This browser version of Python includes the standard library only, not extra packages.
coach.importGeneric.fix: Check the module and the name you import from it.
coach.fileMissing.what: The file does not exist at that path.
coach.fileMissing.fix: Check the file name and capitals. In this course, files live in your browser's virtual disk: write the file first, then read it.
coach.recursion.what: A function kept calling itself without ever stopping.
coach.recursion.fix: Make sure a recursive function has a base case that returns without calling itself again, and that each call gets closer to it.
coach.eof.what: The program asked for input (input()) but there was no more input to give it.
coach.eof.fix: Type an answer when asked. In the fallback mode, write the answers one per line in the input box before running.
coach.overflow.what: A number became too large for this operation.
coach.overflow.fix: Use smaller numbers, or whole numbers (int) which can be as large as you like.
coach.memory.what: The program used more memory than the browser allows.
coach.memory.fix: Work with less data, or check for a loop that keeps growing a list.
coach.assertion.what: An assert statement found something that was not true.
coach.assertion.fix: Check the condition after assert: the values at that moment are not what you expected.
coach.stopIteration.what: next() was called but there is nothing left to give.
coach.stopIteration.fix: Use a for loop, or give next() a default: next(it, None).
coach.permission.what: The program is not allowed to do that to the file.
coach.permission.fix: Check the file mode ('r' to read, 'w' to write) and the path.

lab.title: Practice
lab.help: Predict first, then run, then look at the memory. Wrong guesses go on your watch-list and come back later as short reviews.
lab.predictHelp: Read the code and type exactly what it will print, then press Run and compare.
lab.missed: Not quite. Look at the difference.
lab.firstDiff: First difference on line {line}: expected {want}, got {got}.

lab.solutionLocked: The solution unlocks after you have seen all {n} hints.
lab.solutionNote: Study it, then close it and try writing it yourself.
lab.runnerBusy: The Python engine is starting. This takes a few seconds the first time.
lab.noLabs: No practice for this chapter yet.
mem.title: Memory model
mem.help: Names on the left point to objects on the right. Step through the program to watch them change.
mem.lineReturn: Returning from the function on line {n}
mem.gone: No name points to this object any more, so Python can throw it away.
mem.truncated: Only the first {n} steps are shown.
mem.failed: The program stopped with an error, so the steps end there.
mem.srRef: {name} points to a {type} object with {n} items

review.noneAtAll: Your watch-list is empty. Questions you answer wrong will collect here.
review.done: That is today's review. {right} of {n} right.
review.moved: Moves up. You will see it again in {d} days.
review.reset: Back to the start of the ladder. You will see it again tomorrow.

progress.title: My progress
progress.conceptsHelp: Each bar is an estimate of how well you know a concept, from your answers so far.
progress.empty: Answer some predictions and questions and your concepts will appear here.
progress.aboutText: Tracepad uses a standard learning model (Bayesian knowledge tracing). Each right answer raises the estimate and each wrong one lowers it, more for items that are hard to guess. Answers after using a hint count as practice, not as proof. Nothing here is a grade.
